newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Arabs ask U.N. to consider Israel settlement again.
newsitem.headline: Arabs ask U.N. to consider Israel settlement again.

text.p: The Arab group at the United Nations requested on Monday the reconvening of an emergency special session of the General Assembly to consider Israel's construction of a settlement on occupied territory.

The request was made after Secretary-General Kofi Annan reported that Israel had not abandoned work on the settlement at a site south of Jerusalem that is called Har Homa in Hebrew and Jabal Abu Ghneim in Arabic.

Samsiah Abdul-Majid, spokeswoman for the assembly president, said the request to reconvene April's emergency session was made by Ambassador Nabil Elaraby of Egypt, current chairman of the Arab group. It did not give a specific date.

The Palestine Liberation Organisation's U.N. observer, Nasser Al-Kidwa, said last week a request was in the offing and July 15 was a likely date. Assembly President Razali Ismail of Malaysia will set the date after consulting the chairmen of various regional groups, his spokeswoman said.

The General Assembly, in a resolution adopted on April 25 by a vote of 134 to 3 with 11 abstentions, demanded that Israel immediately halt work on a housing project on the site, captured in the 1967 Middle East war. It also demanded a halt to all other Israeli settlement activities and to all support for "illegal Israeli activities" in the occupied territories.

Annan, in a report he was requested to provide two months after adoption of the resolution, said Israel had not abandoned its construction. This was "viewed as particularly serious" for a variety of political, geographic, demographic and economic reasons, as well as for its effects on the faltering Middle East peace process, he said.
